questions.q: Why doesn't a standard role-hierarchy sharing model fit the Carrow Equipment dealer network?
options: Role hierarchies only work for objects with fewer than 1,200 records
Role hierarchies cannot be used together with Experience Cloud at all
Carrow does not have enough Salesforce licenses to support a role hierarchy
Dealers are independent businesses, not part of Carrow's own organization, so "visibility flowing up a hierarchy" doesn't apply — the actual need is a hard boundary between peer dealers
questions.explain: Role hierarchy assumes an internal reporting structure; dealers need strict peer-to-peer isolation instead, which is a different sharing problem entirely.

questions.q: Why does the design use Salesforce Connect (external objects) for live pricing and inventory instead of replicating that data into Salesforce?
options: Because freshness at the exact moment of ordering matters more here than query performance, and a stale replicated inventory number risks a real fulfillment problem
Because replication is technically impossible for pricing data
Because Salesforce Connect is required by Carrow's SAP contract
Because B2B Commerce cannot function without external objects
questions.explain: The decision is a freshness-versus-performance trade-off specific to this use case — live inventory needs the current SAP state, which replication can't guarantee at the moment of decision.

questions.q: Why does order history get created/owned in Salesforce directly rather than queried live from SAP on every report?
options: Because SAP does not support any form of reporting

Because letting 1,200 dealers' ad hoc Salesforce reports hit SAP live would put open-ended reporting load on a system that shouldn't have to absorb it, when Salesforce's own storage and query engine are the right place for that load
Because order records are legally required to exist only in Salesforce
Because Salesforce Connect cannot read SAP data under any circumstances
questions.explain: This is a load-distribution decision: once an order is placed, the reporting need no longer requires SAP's live state, so handling it in Salesforce avoids burdening the ERP with reporting traffic.

questions.q: Why should the B2B Commerce storefront's pricing configuration be driven by the same Account/territory structure as the sharing model?
options: Because B2B Commerce has no concept of buyer identity at all
Because Salesforce requires all commerce and sharing configuration to live in a single object
Because dealer-specific pricing, catalog visibility, and the sharing model all need to agree on the same definition of "which dealer is this" rather than running as two unrelated systems
Because pricing in B2B Commerce can only be set at the org-wide level, never per dealer
questions.explain: If commerce pricing and sharing are designed as separate workstreams with separate definitions of buyer identity, they can drift apart and produce inconsistent dealer experiences — the fix is a single shared definition.

questions.q: Why does the design support SSO from a dealer's own identity provider rather than requiring every dealer employee to use a Carrow-issued password?
options: Some dealer organizations already run their own identity systems, and supporting their own IdP avoids forcing every individual employee to manage a separate credential
Experience Cloud cannot issue its own passwords under any configuration
SSO is mandatory for every Salesforce org regardless of use case
Carrow-issued passwords are against Salesforce's terms of service for partner users
questions.explain: This is a practical identity-architecture accommodation for dealers that already have their own identity infrastructure, not a platform requirement.
